newsitem.title: ROMANIA: US PRAISES ROMANIA, CONGRATULATES PRESIDENT-ELECT.
newsitem.headline: US PRAISES ROMANIA, CONGRATULATES PRESIDENT-ELECT.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton, congratulating reformist president-elect Emil Constantinescu on his election victory, said Romania had made dramatic progress towards creating a full-fledged democracy.

"It is my great hope that Romania's transformation will deepen under your presidency and that on this basis Romania will become a secure member of the Western democratic community," Clinton said in a letter to Constantinescu.

He praised the record of ex-communist Ion Iliescu, ousted as president in elections at the weekend, by talking of Romania's "dramatic strides" since the fall of communism in 1989 when Iliescu came to power.
In a letter to Iliescu, Clinton said that the "progress recorded during your years as president speaks to the courage and strength of the Romanian people".
Clinton said he looked forward to working with Iliescu in his new role as a member of parliament.
Congratulations also came from eastern neighbour Ukraine, which called for faster negotiations to conclude a friendship treaty blocked by differences dating from World War Two.
Britain also congratulated the new president-elect.

The first Western leader to congratulate Constantinescu was French President Jacques Chirac, who said the outcome showed "the openness of the Romanian people and its aspirations towards Europe". He sent no public message to Iliescu.

In his message on Thursday, Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma said Constantinescu's victory would bolster stability throughout Eastern Europe. He believed a treaty "taking account of post-war realities" would be signed as soon as possible.
Romania concluded a cooperation treaty in September with Hungary after long negotiations over the status of its 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians.

But accords with Russia, Ukraine and Moldova are unsigned largely over Romania's demand that all three denounce the 1939 Nazi-Soviet pact under which the Soviet Union seized Romanian territory. That land is now part of Moldova and Ukraine.
Russian leader Boris Yeltsin congratulated Constantinescu earlier this week and hoped for improved relations.
Outgoing Romanian Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu said on Thursday that the treaty with Ukraine was at an advanced stage.
Ukrainian ambassador Olexander Chaly told Reuters the best way to proceed was to "stress the future, not the past".

Chaly said Ukraine welcomed Constantinescu's campaign pledge to remove all obstacles to a treaty. He called for fresh talks planned for January to be moved forward to next month. REUTER 211731 GMT nov 96
